name: Seafood, all studied species
notes: An average across species and methods. Many fish studies measured the gut, which people usually do not eat, so this probably overstates fillets. Danopoulos 2020 reports 0-2.9 particles/g in fish and 0.1-8.6 in crustaceans.

notes: 4.05 particles per liter, assuming 1 g/mL. Cox 2019 reports 32.27 per liter, so published values differ about 8-fold.

name: Bottled water
samples_note: not stated in the paper text
notes: 94.37 particles per liter, assuming 1 g/mL. Published values vary widely: Kosuth 2018 found 3.57/L in 3 brands. Qian 2024 reported about 240,000 particles/L, about 90% of them nanoplastics, and that figure is disputed in the same journal. It is not used here.

name: Tap water
notes: 5.45 particles per liter, assuming 1 g/mL. Identified by staining and visual inspection, not chemically confirmed.
